title: PHP login with lockout
context: Handles POST /login. Passwords are stored with password_hash. Failures must not reveal whether an email is registered, the session id must be regenerated on success, and an account locks for 15 minutes once it reaches 5 consecutive failed attempts, even when attackers send attempts in parallel. The session is already started.
code: $stmt = $this->db->prepare('SELECT id, password_hash, failed_attempts, locked_until FROM users WHERE email = ?');
$this->db->prepare('UPDATE users SET failed_attempts = 0, locked_until = ? WHERE id = ?')
$this->db->prepare('UPDATE users SET failed_attempts = 0, locked_until = NULL WHERE id = ?')

expected.why: a distinct error for unknown emails lets anyone enumerate registered accounts
the counter is read-modify-written from a stale SELECT, so parallel attempts overwrite each other and bypass the lockout; increment in SQL
the lock triggers on the 6th failure; it must lock once the count reaches 5 (>= 5)
session_regenerate_id(true) is never called, leaving the login open to session fixation
